proposals.title: Exact characterization of generic singleton Gram spectrahedra for sums of squares of quadratics; new general upper bound; m(2)=1 and m(3)=2

source_statement.mathdb_record: Full literal statement read from verified corpus chunk pi-mathdb-full-corpus-inventory-r301/corpus (see dispositions.json entry 404067).
source_statement.statement: What is the maximum number m(n) for which there exists a Euclidean-open subset U of the space of m-tuples of quadratics in n variables such that, for every q=(q_1,...,q_m) in U, the sum sum_i q_i^2 has a singleton Gram spectrahedron? Only known: n-1 <= m(n) < binom(n+1,2).
source_statement.primary_source: Oberwolfach Reports 10.4171/OWR/2023/14, page 52 (https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12697710) as recorded by MathDB. The OWR page itself was NOT retrieved in this lane; ems.press was not accessed.
source_statement.definition_interpretation: Gram spectrahedron of a quartic f is taken in the standard sense: G(f) = {G in Sym_N : G >= 0, v^T G v = f} where v is the vector of ALL N = n(n+1)/2 monomial quadratics and f is quartic. Under the alternative reading (spectrahedron w.r.t. the q_i themselves) the problem is pigeonhole-trivial: the products q_i q_j (i<=j) are m(m+1)/2 quartics in a space of dimension binom(n+3,4), so any nonzero kernel element K (via sum k_ij q_i q_j = 0) gives the 1-parameter family G0 + tK with I + tK >= 0 for small t; hence m(n) <= floor((sqrt(1+8*binom(n+3,4))-1)/2) immediately, which the recorded 'only known' bound would not have missed. The standard reading is therefore the coherent one; this must be confirmed against the OWR text before acceptance.

proposals.quantifiers: n >= 1 integer; m >= 1; q ranges over m-tuples of real quadratic forms; 'Euclidean-open subset of m-tuples with singleton spectrahedron' is the exact MathDB quantifier; m(n) is the maximum such m (m(n) = 0 if none).

new_results.label: T1 (characterization)
new_results.statement: Fix n >= 2 and m >= 1. Let Q = Sym^2(R^n)* (dim N = n(n+1)/2), v the monomial vector, mult: Sym_N -> Sym^4(R^n*) the linear map G |-> v^T G v, kappa(n) := dim ker(mult) = n^2(n^2-1)/12. For an m-tuple q let A be its m x N coefficient matrix (rows = coefficient vectors), G0 = A^T A, and W := ker G0 = (span of the q_i)^perp inside Q. Then the Gram spectrahedron G(f_q), f_q = sum q_i^2, is a singleton {G0} if and only if EVERY nonzero K in ker(mult) restricts to an INDEFINITE quadratic form on W (i.e. takes both strictly positive and strictly negative values on W). In particular the property depends only on U := span(q_i) and is an open condition on the Grassmannian; hence m(n) = max{ m : some m-dimensional U <= Q has the property that every nonzero K in ker(mult) is indefinite on U^perp }.
new_results.proof_sketch: The fiber {G : v^T G v = f_q} equals G0 + ker(mult). If K in ker(mult) is nonzero and v^T K v >= 0 for all v in W = ker G0, then G0 + tK is PSD for all small t > 0 (continuity: on W it is t v^T K v >= 0, off W it is dominated by v^T G0 v > 0), so the spectrahedron is not a singleton; conversely if G0 + tK is PSD for some t > 0 then restriction to W gives t v^T K v >= 0 there. Using -K in ker(mult) as well, singleton is equivalent to: no nonzero K in ker(mult) is PSD or NSD on W, i.e. every nonzero restriction is indefinite. Openness: the set of (projective) K, W with K|_W >= 0 is closed and P(ker) is compact, so the set of good U is open; nonempty open in the Grassmannian pulls back to a Euclidean-open set of m-tuples.

new_results.label: T2 (new unconditional upper bound)
new_results.statement: If w(w+1)/2 <= kappa(n), where w = N - m = dim U^perp, then NO m-tuple is good. Consequently m(n) <= N - w1(n) where w1(n) = min{ w : w(w+1)/2 > n^2(n^2-1)/12 }. Values: m(2) <= 1, m(3) <= 2, m(4) <= 4, m(5) <= 5, m(6) <= 6, m(7) <= 8, m(8) <= 10, m(9) <= 12, m(10) <= 14; asymptotically m(n) <= (1/2 - 1/sqrt(6)) n^2 + O(n) ~ 0.0918 n^2 + n/2. This strictly improves the recorded bound m(n) < binom(n+1,2) for all n >= 3 (and is consistent with it at n = 2).
new_results.proof_sketch: Let L_W = {K in Sym_N : K|_W = 0}, dim L_W = N(N+1)/2 - w(w+1)/2. If dim ker(mult) + dim L_W > N(N+1)/2, i.e. kappa(n) > w(w+1)/2, then ker(mult) ∩ L_W != 0 and any nonzero K in it has K|_W = 0, which is not indefinite: not good. If equality holds w(w+1)/2 = kappa(n), then either ker ∩ L_W != 0 (not good) or the restriction map ker(mult) -> Sym_W is injective between spaces of the same dimension kappa(n), hence surjective, so some K restricts to a nonzero PSD matrix ww^T: not good.

new_results.label: T3 (m(2) = 1, self-contained)
new_results.statement: m(2) = 1. Upper bound: T2. Lower bound: for n = 2, ker(mult) is 1-dimensional, spanned by K0 = E_13 + E_31 - 2 E_22 in the monomial basis (x^2, xy, y^2), i.e. v^T K0 v = 2 x^2 y^2 - 2 (xy)^2 = 0; K0 has eigenvalues 1, -1, -2. For a generic 1-dimensional U (e.g. U = span of any quadratic whose orthogonal complement is a generic plane), K0 restricts to an indefinite form on U^perp (the bad planes {W : K0|_W <= 0} form a proper closed subset, e.g. W = span(xy, y^2) is bad while generic planes are good); hence an open set of single quadratics q have singleton Gram spectrahedra.
new_results.note: Concrete bad/good distinction executed by hand: for W = span(xy, y^2), v^T K0 v = -2 b^2 <= 0 (semi-definite, bad); for generic planes the restriction takes both signs. Explicit witness that even m = 1 is sharp in disguise: for n = 2, m = 2 ALWAYS fails (W is 1-dimensional; K0 and -K0 give a PSD direction regardless), matching m(2) = 1 = n - 1.

new_results.label: T4 (m(3) = 2)
new_results.statement: m(3) = 2. Upper bound m(3) <= 2 is unconditional by T2 (kappa(3) = 6; w = 3 fails both cases of the T2 argument). Lower bound m(3) >= 2 is the recorded bound n - 1 <= m(n) of the MathDB statement, independently consistent with the typical-case theorem of arXiv:2305.06860 (unique decomposition provable for m <= n-1).
new_results.status: complete modulo the recorded lower bound; a self-contained exact verification of m(3) >= 2 for one explicit 2-dim U is specified under decisive_calculation (planned, not executed here).

proposals.mechanism: Tangent-space characterization of the PSD cone at the particular fiber point G0 = A^T A (interior directions), combined with a linear-dimension count of the fixed relation space ker(mult) against the restriction target Sym_W. No numeric search, no inequality crunching: the upper bound is pure dimension counting plus the sign symmetry K <-> -K of the linear kernel.

proposals.certificate_size: Proofs are elementary exact linear algebra; roughly 3-4 pages. No large certificates. The planned m(3) >= 2 verification yields a small exact rational witness (one U, one rank computation, finitely many sign checks).
proposals.formalization: Lean endpoint feasible without heavy machinery: needs real finite-dimensional linear algebra (dimension counting, restriction of quadratic forms), an eigenvalue computation for a fixed 3x3 integer matrix, and the elementary PSD-cone tangent argument. No analysis, no topology beyond Euclidean openness of finitely determined conditions. Only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound expected. Estimated effort: moderate (the dimension-counting bookkeeping is the main cost).

found: arXiv:2305.06860 (Blomenhofer, 'Unique powers-of-forms decompositions from simple Gram spectrahedra'): typical-case uniqueness for m <= n-1 and evidence for m = Theta(n^2); no upper bound on m(n), no exact m(n), no characterization of singleton spectrahedra. objections_and_risks: Interpretation risk: the brief fixes the standard (all-monomial) Gram spectrahedron reading; the OWR 2023/14 p.52 text must be retrieved to confirm (ems.press not accessed in this lane).
The m(3) = 2 lower bound currently rests on the recorded n-1 <= m(n) plus a reported typical-case theorem, not on a proof body read here.

Novelty of T2 is not guaranteed: the tangent-space argument is elementary once seen, and the OWR authors may have known stronger bounds than they recorded; chronology of any public counterpart must be compared before credit.
If the intended reading is instead 'w.r.t. the q_i', the problem collapses to a dimension count (noted above) and this whole brief is void.
proposals.credit_limit: At most: (a) the characterization T1, (b) the upper bound T2, (c) exact m(2) = 1 and m(3) = 2. NOT claimed: full determination of m(n) for n >= 4.
